candidates.title: Canada Malting plant could collapse at any moment, engineering report says
candidates.description: According to an engineering firm's report, the Canada Malting plant in Montreal's Sud-Ouest borough could collapse at any moment. The report states “controlled demolition is the only possible, safe and rational solution to eliminate the critical danger that this building represents.”
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Belleville police investigating antisemitic flyers less than 2 weeks after synagogue attack
candidates.description: Police in Belleville, Ont., say they're investigating antisemitic flyers being distributed in the city less than two weeks after a gunman was killed attempting to attack a local synagogue on Yom Kippur.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Latest N.L. tourism ad boasts Josh Hartnett, but are real fishermen the true catch?
candidates.description: Josh Hartnett, who spent time in parts of Newfoundland filming the Netflix series Below, is front and the centre of a new ad promoting tourism in the province. But some fishermen say the Hollywood star has nothing on them.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Toronto board of trade urges province to reform housing regulations
candidates.description: The Toronto Region Board of Trade is urging the province to amend zoning and building code rules as it says Ontario is on pace to fall well short of its goal of getting at least 1.5 million new homes built by 2031.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Poll suggests slight majority of UCP voters favours separation as party stares down ‘tough days’ ahead
candidates.description: A new poll suggests the group with the highest level of support for Alberta separation is supporters of the United Conservative Party, trumping other groups, including those defined by age, religiosity and education.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Non-member beneficiaries of Robinson Huron Treaty settlement have mixed views over compensation amount
candidates.description: Members of a group of Robinson Huron Treaty settlement beneficiaries who have yet to receive compensation from a historic settlement for unpaid past annuities have mixed opinions on the amount offered to them. The case involves the retroactive amount owed to the 21 First Nations for access to natural resources in the treaty territory, covering about 92,000 square kilometres to the north and east of Lake Huron.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta men convicted in Coutts border blockade lose appeals
candidates.description: The Alberta Court of Appeal has dismissed the appeals of two leaders of the 2022 Coutts border blockade who were convicted of mischief and weapons offences.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New Indigenous art exhibit in Hamilton places Mother Earth where Sir John A. Macdonald statue once stood
candidates.description: A new art exhibit in Gore Park asks passersby to reflect on the legacy of Canada's first prime minister and repossesses the space where his statue once stood in Hamilton. It was installed for the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation Wednesday and will be in the downtown park until the weekend.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Months after delay and ‘long, hard, painful’ path, Innu history exhibit opens in Labrador
candidates.description: Three months after initially scheduled, the Innu Pakassiun exhibit at the abrador Interpretation Centre in North West River has opened — a moment Innu Nation Grand Chief Jodie Ashini says was filled with emotion and deep significance.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge dismisses sexual assault case against Trailer Park Boys star Mike Smith
candidates.description: A sexual assault case against Trailer Park Boys actor Mike Smith was dropped in Dartmouth provincial court on Thursday. The complainant says the trial was dismissed because she was "unwilling to sacrifice" her mental health to go through the criminal justice process.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadian Olympian Claire Thompson retires from PWHL to pursue medical career
candidates.description: Defender Claire Thompson, one of Canada's top women's hockey players, is retiring from the sport to become a doctor. The 28-year-old played with the PWHL's Vancouver Goldeneyes last season.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why children in government care face a higher risk of sexual exploitation
candidates.description: Young people who are in government care can be prime targets for sexual exploitation, as demonstrated by recent cases in Nova Scotia courts. According to a senior Crown prosecutor, sexual predators found the children by lurking near group homes or scoping them out on social media.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Is this Quebec riding encroaching on Newfoundland and Labrador? Depends who you ask
candidates.description: Looking at Quebec’s electoral map, the riding of Duplessis, located in the province’s Côte-Nord region, might not stand out in the minds of the majority of Quebecers. But a closer look at the district’s boundaries — as they appear on the Élections Québec’s electoral map — reveals a long-standing grievance held by Quebec.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Vancouver band cancels Charlottetown show after venue denied transgender member washroom access
candidates.description: A Vancouver punk band that was set to play in Charlottetown this past weekend cancelled its show after a transgender band member was stopped from using the women's washroom at the venue.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Overnight, Meta deleted all her accounts. AI customer service won’t let her reach a human
candidates.description: Toronto resident Jasmine Ault says Meta disabled her accounts overnight, without giving her a reason, and that she's been unable to get past their AI chatbots to speak to a human to resolve the error. Experts say without regulation enforcing the right to speak to a human, this will keep happening.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: N.S. volunteer fire departments sound alarm over fuel costs
candidates.description: The soaring cost of diesel is becoming a growing concern for Nova Scotia's volunteer fire departments who rely on the fuel to run the majority of their trucks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Former soldier exposes how Canadian white supremacist group recruits members
candidates.description: Second Sons Canada describes itself as a "men's nationalist club" dedicated to fitness and preserving Canada's heritage, but a former military member who attempted to join the group says he only learned about its true nature — which included adoration for Hitler, neo-Nazis and hatred for Jews — when he met them in person and was presented with a confidentiality contract.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Saskatchewan mayor stepping down now that 'Queen of Canada' cult is gone
candidates.description: When Brad Miller signed up to be mayor of Richmound, Sask., he never imagined his tiny southwestern village would be overrun by a cult. After three years and many sleepless nights, the cult is finally gone, and Miller will resign on Oct. 15.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: UCP MLA says he’s voted in favour of Alberta holding binding referendum on independence
candidates.description: Red Deer-South MLA Jason Stephan says he has voted in favour of Alberta’s government proceeding with a legally binding referendum on separation, but adds he hopes to see Canada united if Alberta is “treated fairly” as a result.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What we know so far about the midair FlyDubai attack
candidates.description: The motivations of a FlyDubai pilot, and what weapon was used, are among the foremost questions surrounding how a flight bound for Israel from the United Arab Emirates avoided disaster Wednesday after a cockpit incident.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Renee Good's family sues U.S. government, ICE officer and others over Minneapolis killing
candidates.description: Lawsuits filed by Renee Good's family allege wrongful death, conspiracy and other violations in the 37-year-old's fatal shooting by a U.S. immigration officer during an immigration crackdown in January.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What happened in Tennessee's failed execution of Christa Pike and what comes next?
candidates.description: It remains unclear why the execution of Christa Pike, who was sentenced to death for the 1995 killing of a classmate at age 18, failed. Pike was given two doses of lethal injections Wednesday, according to observers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Putin warns West not to escalate, claims concerns about Russia's Kaliningrad region
candidates.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Thursday the world was living through a dangerous moment and warned the West not to escalate a standoff ‌over Ukraine by threatening the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, which Moscow has made clear it would defend with nuclear weapons if necessary.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.A.E. announces investigation into FlyDubai stabbing
candidates.description: The United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has ordered an investigation into the ‌stabbing aboard FlyDubai Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, ​which was diverted ​and landed in Saudi Arabia after a struggle ​in the cockpit, the state news agency ‌reported Thursday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: This is how fast Swiss glaciers, the 'water tower of Europe,' are melting away
candidates.description: Glaciers in Switzerland lost 5.5 per cent of their ice volume this year, the second-biggest percentage drop on record. It's part of a trend that could have big impacts in a country reliant on hydropower and which acts as the 'water tower of Europe,' feeding its major rivers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tennessee governor orders outside review after death row inmate Christa Pike survives execution attempt
candidates.description: Christa Pike, convicted of murdering a classmate three decades ago, survived Tennessee's effort to execute her by means of lethal injection late on Wednesday, prison officials and her lawyers said, foiling the state's first attempt to put a woman to death in two centuries.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Families of Canadian mining firm workers kidnapped in Mexico plan to file RCMP complaint
candidates.description: The families of the workers of a Canadian mining firm kidnapped earlier this year by a suspected cartel commando squad in the violence-torn Mexican state of Sinaloa plan to file an RCMP complaint against the Vancouver-based company, their lawyer says.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says 'very bad' Canada is being 'taught a little lesson' as trade action escalates
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump's war of words with Canada continued Wednesday as he veered off a prepared script at an event marking Hispanic Heritage Month in the States to chastise Canadian leaders for being what he called "very bad."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Passengers foil bid to crash Dubai-Tel Aviv flight after co-pilot stabbed pilot, Israel says
candidates.description: Passengers on a FlyDubai flight reached Israel safely on Wednesday after passengers and crew foiled a co-pilot's attempt to crash the aircraft, Israeli officials said, in a struggle that began when he stabbed the pilot and sent the jet plunging.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: After day of delays, witnesses say Tennessee unable to carry out execution of Christa Pike
candidates.description: Tennessee officials were unable to carry out the execution of Christa Gail Pike for a 1995 murder on Wednesday, media witnesses said, after the lethal injection was halted for hours as courts considered a last-minute appeal.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Pentagon confirms U.S. military will cut 20% of generals and admirals
candidates.description: U.S. War Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed Wednesday that the U.S. military will cut 20 per cent of its generals and admirals as he made a series of announcements in what he called his "state of the force" address.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why pro-Trump ads — paid for with public money — are airing on U.S. TV
candidates.description: With crucial midterm elections just weeks away, the White House is using taxpayer funds to air campaign-style TV ads featuring U.S. President Donald Trump.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How AI hacked the Australian government and almost got away with it | About That
candidates.description: OpenAI says one of its models, while in testing, went rogue and hacked an official Australian government website in a security breach that went undetected for months. Andrew Chang explains what we know about the hack and why Australian authorities say the manner in which they learned about the incident was 'entirely inadequate.' Images provided by The Canadian Press, Reuters, Adobe Stock and Getty Images
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: G20 trade ministers are meeting in Wisconsin. Many will be discussing deals without their U.S. host
candidates.description: Most of the officials attending the G20 trade ministers' meeting in Milwaukee, Wisc., find themselves in challenging positions, largely because of U.S. President Donald Trump's global tariff agenda. It makes for a potentially unusual summit, with high-level meetings on the sidelines where different countries discuss plans to work around the host.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russian airstrikes kill at least 7, damage infrastructure in Ukraine
candidates.description: Russia unleashed an air campaign against Ukraine's energy grid on Wednesday, ‌hitting power facilities and infrastructure around Kyiv and other regions in what Ukraine's prime minister said was the heaviest combined attack on energy sites in months.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Eiffel Tower chief to step down after female staff excluded during Hindu delegation visit
candidates.description: The head of the company that runs the Eiffel Tower will step down at the end of the year after female staff at the landmark building in Paris were excluded during a visit by a Hindu religious group.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Princess Diana’s brother says ‘she will never be extinguished’
candidates.description: Charles Spencer has written a new book about the late Princess Diana, and Buckingham Palace is not impressed. In conversation with CBC Radio The Current host Matt Galloway he offers an intimate look at his sister’s character and talks about the tense moments with Prince Charles in the aftermath of the tragic 1997 Paris car crash.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says top tech firms have signed accord to 'self-police' AI development
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has signed a voluntary pact with artificial intelligence companies to "self-police" the technology's development.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: West Coast oil pipeline becomes 1st project designated in national interest
candidates.description: The federal and Alberta governments have announced that a proposed pipeline carrying one million barrels of oil a day from Alberta to the B.C. coast has become the first project designated in the national interest.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: AI agents tried to hack Library and Archives Canada website, research firm says
candidates.description: AI agents tried to hack into a Library and Archives Canada website, according to a report by artificial intelligence research firm Transluce.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Stelco's U.S. owner touts right to idle operations at Hamilton steel plant as PM vows legal action
candidates.description: The chief executive officer of Stelco’s American parent company says he has every legal right to idle production at a steel mill in Hamilton as Prime Minister Mark Carney threatens legal action.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: After 'doom and gloom' decade, Fort McMurray readies for a boom
candidates.description: The Alberta community synonymous with meteoric oil booms and crippling busts is now staring down another potential wave of economic fortune.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney announces $1.2B in funding to protect oceans as major projects loom
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced $1.2 billion in federal funding for ocean protections Tuesday, as the country moves toward decisions on a new pipeline to the West Coast and the expansion of a major port in Metro Vancouver.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What happened in the failed execution of Christa Pike - and what next?
candidates.description: The convicted killer is in hospital in Tennessee after surviving two lethal injections, in a case that has raised many questions.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Netanyahu says Flydubai attacker had 'Islamist radical indoctrination'
candidates.description: Israel's prime minister says the pilot who tried to take over the Flydubai plane clearly intended to "down the plane".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Putin warns West that Russia is ready to use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad
candidates.description: The Russian leader insists Moscow is "not threatening anyone" and is merely responding to statements by Western leaders.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Trump's AI rebrand causes 'unprecedented' demand for Slovenian website names
candidates.description: The president wants AI to be called super intelligence - or SI - the same initials used by Slovenian domains.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Russian dissident Garry Kasparov says US warned him of danger to his life
candidates.description: "My family and I will not truly be safe as long as Putin is in power," says the former chess world champion.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Kanye West's Russia shows officially cancelled after weeks of uncertainty
candidates.description: Chaos has surrounded the St Petersburg shows since the stadium said it had not agreed to host the rapper.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Algeria introduces death penalty for arsonists after deadly wildfires
candidates.description: It is estimated more than 200 people have died in blazes in the north-east of the country over the summer.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: K-pop star convicted of violating military service law
candidates.description: The member of K-pop band Winner was given a suspended prison sentence for repeated absences from his national service work.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Explosions heard in Ethiopia's capital after drone flights banned
candidates.description: It comes a week after fighting erupted north of the capital between the army and a new alliance of armed groups.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Flydubai passenger describes hugging his children as plane nosedived during attack
candidates.description: Adam Polovincik tells the BBC he told his young children "everything is going to be all right" as flight plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m).

candidates.title: Rosenberg: Putin shows no sign of stopping the war as Russia doubles down on Ukraine
candidates.description: A foreign policy speech by the Russian president will be keenly watched, but all signs point to the full-scale invasion continuing.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.description: Beijing has cracked down on AI chatbots that can replicate human relationships. Experts are asking if this is the right thing to do.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Inside India's forest villages, where a dangerous mix of crises led to 32 child deaths
candidates.description: At least 32 children have died in India's Balaghat district since May amid outbreaks of measles and malaria.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Three takeaways from Trump's 'Super Intelligence' summit
candidates.description: The meeting at the White House came as some tech bosses and experts have called for tighter rules around AI.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Why are students protesting at schools in France?
candidates.description: The BBC's Hugh Schofield is in Paris as a wave of school protests over overcrowded classes and teacher shortages spreads across France.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Couple describes relief at rescue after whale destroys their yacht
candidates.description: Jeremy and Jemma Cooper were 500 miles off the coast of New Zealand when their yacht, the Tai Tam, collided with a sperm whale.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Luxury prison in Indonesia demolished after public outcry
candidates.description: Indonesian lawmakers on Wednesday ordered the demolition of a controversial luxury compound inside a penitentiary near the capital.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: AI boom could trigger market shocks, Bank of England boss warns
candidates.description: Andrew Bailey says the central bank is watching the waves of cash being invested in artificial intelligence "very carefully".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: The AI telling farmers when to harvest
candidates.description: Will farmers want AI tools to help judge when to pick fruit, or is their own intuition enough?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons
candidates.description: Mindgard said it discovered in July that Kimi models K2.6 and K3 Swarm could evade developer's safety limits.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: SpaceX launches crew to ISS
candidates.description: The Falcon 9 rocket blasted off from Cape Canaveral with two Americans, a Russian and a Canadian who will spend up to six months aboard the International Space Station.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Meet '89 Backpack', the chunky bear who won Fat Bear Week
candidates.description: The brown bear, described by one supporter as having both the "chonk and the badonk", will shortly enter hibernation, which can last up to six months.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Moment a government building collapses into a river in Nepal amid floods
candidates.description: The municipality building in Baglung was left teetering on an unstable ledge due to floods before it fell into a river.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What a Pearly King taught me about Cockney rhyming slang and East London history
candidates.description: In mother-of-pearl suits, the Pearly Kings used to canvass East London for charity. The most famous one, George Major, died in August. A look back on this larger-than-life figure and the Pearly King tradition.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Passengers recount chaos on Tel Aviv flight. And, FBI probes employee-data hack
candidates.description: What we know so far about the tense moments aboard a Tel Aviv-bound flight. And, the FBI investigates a cyberattack involving sensitive employee data.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Picanha, prices and politics: What Brazil's favorite steak says about the election
candidates.description: President Lula promised Brazilians four years ago they'd be able to afford picanha again. Now, as he seeks another term, the price of the country's favorite cut of beef is telling a different story.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What life under U.S. sanctions looks like for one ICC judge
candidates.description: Kimberly Prost, a Canadian judge at the International Criminal Court, says U.S. sanctions disrupted her daily life. She is still hearing cases and challenging the sanctions in court.

candidates.title: Swiss glaciers suffer another year of record ice loss
candidates.description: Switzerland's glaciers are disappearing at a record pace. More than 5% of their ice has vanished this year alone — threatening water supplies, ecosystems and communities across Europe.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Greetings from Syria, where time seems to melt as a glassmaker braves scorching temps
candidates.description: As a Syrian glassmaker created his wares in Damascus, watching his craft reminded this reporter to slow down and enjoy the moment.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How Ukrainians are coping with new, more deadly Russian attacks
candidates.description: Zanny Minton Beddoes, The Economist's editor in chief , just visited Ukraine. She says, despite all its drone weaponry, Kyiv is under extraordinary bombardment, as Russia tries to make it unlivable.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A midair stabbing on a flight to Israel is being investigated as possible terrorism
candidates.description: FlyDubai said the motives behind the incident were unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu described it as "a serious security incident."
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. forces exit Iraq amid Iran war. And, SCOTUS revives Trump deportation policy
candidates.description: The U.S. has withdrawn its final troops from Iraq, leaving its defense future uncertain. And, the Supreme Court has sided for now with the Trump administration on third-country deportations.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The U.S. military withdraws from Iraq over 2 decades after its invasion
candidates.description: 23 years after the United States military invaded Iraq, sparking an insurgency and a civil war, the U.S. has withdrawn its forces, as the country still tries to combat Iranian influence.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Breweries adapt as tastes in beer change
candidates.description: The craft beer market is saturated and tastes are changing. Brewers are coming with innovative ways to attract customers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Google launches Project Suncatcher, a step towards AI data centers in space
candidates.description: The fridge-size satellite with AI chips on board is part of Project Suncatcher, the company's moonshot effort to put AI data centers in space and harness solar energy.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Egg prices have tumbled since Trump returned to office. Here's why
candidates.description: Agriculture experts say high egg prices were the result of severe avian flu outbreaks, but the Trump administration's tariffs and the war with Iran have also put pressure on farmers.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trade tensions mean fewer Canadians flocking to South Florida
candidates.description: This South Florida community is typically a refuge for Canadians fleeing cold weather, but trade tensions between the United States and Canada mean fewer are coming.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A startup wants to build a massive nuclear-powered data center on public land in Utah
candidates.description: Valar Atomics wants to place over 450 reactors on more than 9,500 acres in Utah to power a huge data center project.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: One year after the end of the EV tax credit, is the future still electric?
candidates.description: Congress got rid of a $7,500 federal tax credit for new electric vehicle buyers. One year later, are people still buying EVs?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 'It's a nightmare.' Former refugee, professor on Trump's new Medicaid policy
candidates.description: Starting Oct. 1, many immigrants who are here legally lose their Medicaid coverage because of the Republican budget bill passed last year.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: A new California law bans child marriage. What's the global outlook on the practice?
candidates.description: The governor of California has signed into law a ban on child marriage. What is the status of other efforts to ban the practice? And do bans prove effective?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump administration reverses stance on integration of people with disabilities
candidates.description: Disability rights advocates are angered by the latest reversal but are rallying behind proposed legislation and working with states to strengthen protections for community integration.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: After failed execution, health workers say Tennessee's method flouts medical ethics
candidates.description: After a botched lethal injection in May, dozens of Tennessee medical professionals told the governor that healthcare professionals shouldn't help with executions, no matter the method.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Travel plans? Here's what to know as measles exposures reach trains and games
candidates.description: Measles is traveling, with outbreaks in Pennsylvania, Ohio and New York, and exposures on transportation and in sports. What should you know before getting on a plane or train?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What's behind HHS claims that gender-affirming care 'may' radicalize
candidates.description: The report is the agency's latest effort to chip away at trust in established health care models for transgender people. Critics say it frames transgender identity as illegitimate or even dangerous.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Montana starts enforcing Medicaid work requirements on Oct 1. Patients are confused
candidates.description: In most states, people with Medicaid coverage will have to prove they're working, volunteering or studying, starting Jan. 1. But Montana is starting that early, and it's sowing confusion and anxiety.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: They were promised protection. Instead, these kids with disabilities died in foster care
candidates.description: Disabled kids make up the largest group in foster care. They have the worst outcomes. They stay in foster care longest. They're the most likely to die.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Drugs are widely used to sedate dementia patients. Her sons wanted to keep her off them
candidates.description: Potent sedating medications are often used on agitated people with dementia in long-term care facilities despite federal efforts to discourage them. A clash over whether to drug a Michigan woman illuminates the wrenching decisions families and guardians face.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Rural voters support MAHA movement, but feel little impact, poll finds
candidates.description: A new poll from KFF-AP shows that rural voters support the Make America Healthy Again movement, but they don't think it's had a positive impact on their lives.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ranking-Aware Prompt Optimization for Multimodal Clinical Diagnosis
candidates.description: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are rapidly advancing clinical diagnosis, yet their adaptation pipelines remain anchored to accuracy-based objectives. Clinical data are heavily class-imbalanced: a constant-majority predictor can score above 90% accuracy while being clinically useless. We therefore evaluate and optimize for AUROC, a threshold-free score that ranks positives above negatives and is invariant to class balance. We focus on prompt optimization in MLLMs. Reflective methods such as GEPA use a binary scores matrix with one row per evaluation instance and one column per candidate prompt; cells record per-instance correctness, so the column average is accuracy and drives candidate selection. We introduce pair-level Pareto prompt evolution (Ranking-PE), which replaces each correctness row with a pairwise-ordering row over (positive, negative) instance pairs: the cell is 1 if the candidate scores the positive higher than the paired negative. The column average then equals empirical AUROC (by the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney identity). We apply this swap at all three layers the prompt evolution search reads from - the scores matrix that decides Pareto dominance, the per-example feedback to the reflection LM, and final candidate selection - at no extra model calls and with no surrogate loss. Across three diseases on MIMIC, accuracy-based prompt evolution can degrade ranking; Ranking-PE reverses this, beating the accuracy-based recipe by +5.8 AUROC pp on fine-tuned Qwen3-VL-8B and +16.2 pp on MedGemma-4B. Ablations examine each design component and show that a medical-grade visual backbone - via vision-encoder-tuned SFT or medical pretraining - is a prerequisite that prompt search cannot replace - our recipe extends reflective prompt evolution from text-only data to multimodal clinical decision-making.
candidates.author: Tian Xia, Minghao Liu, Yiqing Liang, Laixi Shi, Jiayun Wang

candidates.title: Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization
candidates.description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has improved the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs), yet their predictions remain sensitive to task-irrelevant prompt features. We investigate this sensitivity through semifactual prompt interventions that preserve the underlying problem and its answer. Our analysis reveals substantial variation in token-level sensitivity and shows that suppressing high-drift token candidates during decoding improves reasoning accuracy without updating model weights. These findings highlight a limitation of Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), which assigns the same outcome-derived advantage to every response token and may reinforce potential spurious dependence alongside useful reasoning. Motivated by this observation, we introduce Semifactual Credit-Augmented Policy Optimization (SCAPO), a causally inspired variant of GRPO that incorporates semifactual stability into token-level credit assignment. SCAPO measures token probability drift for fixed responses under semifactual interventions and uses normalized stability scores to reduce advantages for relatively unstable tokens during early training, while granting no additional credit for stability alone. On Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-1.7B-Base, SCAPO improves AIME 2024-2026 accuracy over GRPO by 5.63 and 4.17 percentage points, respectively. At both model scales, SCAPO achieves the best results on most evaluated mathematics benchmarks and all evaluated out-of-distribution benchmarks among the compared methods. These results suggest that semifactual stability provides an effective training signal for improving reasoning and generalization through finer-grained credit assignment in RLVR. The code is available at https://github.com/DtYXs/SCAPO.
candidates.author: Junshu Pan, Zhizhang Fu, Shulin Huang, Yiran Ding, Zifan Cheng, Wenqi Shao, Qiaosheng Zhang, Yue Zhang

candidates.title: ViTeX-Bench: Benchmarking High-Fidelity Video Scene Text Editing
candidates.description: Recent video generation is increasingly realistic and controllable, yet video editing remains less developed, particularly for precise local edits that must preserve the original scene dynamics. Video scene text editing replaces text on scene surfaces, such as storefront signs, whiteboards, and product labels, while preserving the surrounding content, motion, and camera dynamics. Although scene text editing is well studied for images, video scene text editing that achieves high visual quality, temporal consistency, and edit locality remains underexplored. Existing resources offer limited paired real-video data, and general video-editing metrics do not directly measure whether the requested text remains correct over time. We introduce ViTeX-Bench, a benchmark suite comprising ViTeX-Dataset and a three-axis evaluation protocol. The dataset contains 387 real-world 720p videos with text-region masks and editing instructions: 230 provide reviewed, pipeline-generated paired edits for training, and 157 form a frozen evaluation split. The protocol evaluates text correctness, visual and temporal quality, and edit locality through 13 metrics, with one primary metric per axis and a Pareto comparison of their trade-offs. OCR calibration, human evaluation, and annotation-sensitivity analyses support the interpretation of these scores. Across eight baselines from four editing families, accurate text, temporal stability, and scene preservation remain difficult to achieve together. We also release ViTeX-Edit-14B, an open-source reference editor fine-tuned on the paired training split with motion-aligned glyph-video conditioning. It achieves CharAcc 0.688, the highest mean among the evaluated video-native editors, and the lowest comparable text-crop Warp among raw editor outputs. ViTeX-Bench provides a reproducible foundation for studying these trade-offs in video scene text editing.
candidates.author: Xinghao Chen, Xiangbo Gao, Jiongze Yu, Yuheng Wu, Zhengzhong Tu

candidates.title: AssemblyWorld: Rethinking 3D Assembly with General-Purpose Agents
candidates.description: The task of 3D assembly requires translating an understanding of parts and their relationships into precise spatial arrangements. Can pretrained general-purpose agents assemble objects through visual interaction without additional assembly-specific fine-tuning? To investigate this question, we introduce AssemblyWorld, an interactive 3D environment in which agents inspect rendered views and manipulate supplied rigid parts, guided by images or assembly manuals when available. Agents perceive part geometry through 2D views rather than direct access to mesh vertices or faces, while their resulting assemblies are evaluated geometrically. Building on this environment, we construct AssemblyWorldBench, comprising 100 assembly tasks across 80 objects spanning furniture, industrial assembly, and fracture reassembly. Evaluating eight agent systems reveals substantial differences in their capabilities. The strongest system achieves 80.9% part accuracy but 59.4% complete-assembly success. The evaluated open-source systems lag substantially behind their stronger closed-source peers in both execution reliability and assembly accuracy. Analyses of visual references, interaction trajectories, and failures show how agents revise assemblies while leaving residual positioning errors. AssemblyWorld provides a common setting for both assessing the capabilities of interactive assembly agents and characterizing the gap between approximate structure recovery and precise reconstruction.
candidates.author: Jiahao Zhang, Yeying Fan, Moitreya Chatterjee, Suhas Lohit, Bernhard Egger, Tim K. Marks, Anoop Cherian, Stephen Gould

candidates.title: Ego4WAM: What Matters When Scaling Egocentric Human Data for Robot Learning?
candidates.description: Egocentric human data provides a scalable source of experience for robot learning, but varies substantially in human-robot alignment, behavioral coverage, and available supervision. Existing work shows favorable scaling with increasing human data, but it remains unclear which data properties drive downstream robot gains and how to use such data throughout the training pipeline. We present a systematic study of egocentric human data with different alignment and supervision under a unified world-action model framework. With the model backbone fixed, we disentangle the effects of human-robot alignment, data duration and task diversity, action supervision, and data usage strategies. We find that aligned human demonstrations substantially improve out-of-distribution generalization and reduce target-task robot data requirements; data duration and task diversity affect downstream capabilities differently; and video-only supervision remains effective without action labels, providing a strong foundation for subsequent video-action training. We validate these findings through closed-loop policy evaluation on both real robots and RoboDojo. Rather than treating data duration as the sole scaling axis, Ego4WAM shows how alignment, task diversity, available supervision, and usage strategy jointly shape the value of egocentric human data for robot learning.
candidates.author: Zhihao Sun, Liu Liu, Xinjiang Wang, Haoyi Jiang, Wei Feng, Huiqiang Zhang, Xiaosong Jia, Zhizhong Su, Zuxuan Wu

candidates.title: EvoDuet: Bilevel Co-Evolution of Web Searching and Task Solving for Scientific Discovery
candidates.description: Evolutionary search with large language models (LLMs) can stall when progress requires external knowledge the model lacks. Supplying relevant documents helps, but simply adding web search tool can keep returning the same pages as solutions change. We introduce EvoDuet, a bi-level optimization method that co-evolves solutions and search queries with fixed model parameters. At each iteration, a retrieval gate lets the LLM assess its knowledge gap and choose to retrieve new documents, reuse stored ones, or proceed without them. An inner loop refines queries and ranks documents by the solution scores they are predicted to yield; an outer loop generates candidates in parallel from these documents and records the evaluated outcomes for later searches. Across 21 optimization tasks with one candidate per iteration, EvoDuet raises OpenEvolve's normalized discovery gain from 74.1% to 78.0% with GPT-5.6-Luna and from 61.3% to 82.3% with Gemini-3.8-Flash, whereas Qwen3.5-9B does not benefit. Our best runs surpass the previously reported best scores on eight tasks, including Swap Reduction on Q20 and Rosetta, and match them on three more. EvoDuet also improves with other scaffolds (e.g., Top-K, EvoX) on Sums/Diffs and Denoising, demonstrating its applicability across evolutionary search scaffolds.
candidates.author: Young-Jun Lee, Jinheon Baek, Soyeong Jeong, Minki Kang, Seungyeon Jwa, Jonghyun Choi, Seungho Han, Dongyeop Kang

candidates.title: Turbo Harness: Instance-Adaptive Harness Optimization
candidates.description: Automating the search for effective harnesses is an important step toward enabling agents to recursively self-improve. Existing harness optimizations typically produce a single global harness that is applied uniformly across task instances. However, a harness that works well on average may not be optimal for every instance. We introduce Turbo Harness, a framework that can adapt a globally optimized harness to each instance by reusing information generated during the original optimization process. Specifically, Turbo Harness recycles artifacts produced during a completed global harness optimization run, and summarizes them into a structured playbook. We train a harness editor to leverage this prior optimization experience to generate instance-specific patches to the global harness. At inference time, the editor uses the instance and the playbook to construct a tailored harness in which the execution model operates. Through numerical experiments, we show that Turbo Harness consistently outperforms existing harness optimization baselines across seven benchmarks spanning interactive agent tasks, software engineering, and long-horizon terminal tasks.
candidates.author: Tunyu Zhang, Hao Wang, Kai Xu, Dimitris N. Metaxas

candidates.title: WorldAuditBench: Interactive 3D World Auditing with Multimodal Agents
candidates.description: As interactive 3D worlds are increasingly used to study intelligent behavior, it becomes important to develop efficient pipelines for identifying anomalies in these simulated environments, such as floating objects, traversable walls, or objects inconsistent with the surrounding scene. Multimodal AI systems, including vision-language models (VLMs) and vision-language-action models (VLAs), have shown potential for automating this task. However, 3D world auditing is complex, requiring the close coupling of two distinct capabilities: action, to navigate the 3D world and search for anomalies systematically and efficiently; and visual reasoning, to understand the environment and identify anomalies from multimodal observations. It remains largely unexplored whether multimodal agents can effectively couple these two capabilities, using visual reasoning to identify potential anomalies while taking actions to validate them. In this paper, we introduce WorldAuditBench, a benchmark for 3D world auditing comprising 213 anomaly tasks across 13 environments built with Unreal Engine 5 and Three.js, spanning five anomaly families. We evaluate five frontier models under a fixed exploration budget using two auditing paradigms: VLA-based exploration followed by VLM-based anomaly identification, and an end-to-end VLM agent in which visual reasoning directly guides action selection. Across the evaluated models and two paradigms, success rates range from 6.6% to 42.3%, substantially below human performance (83.4%). Through the task of world auditing, WorldAuditBench provides a testbed for studying how multimodal agents couple action and visual reasoning in interactive 3D environments, while highlighting current limitations in their ability to gather and interpret evidence during exploration.
candidates.author: Ziyan Jiang, Jingbo Yang, Jiabao Ji, Yujian Liu, Qiucheng Wu, Tommi Jaakkola, Yang Zhang, Shiyu Chang

candidates.title: Cogentic: Multi-Agent Orchestration for Automated Proof Discovery
candidates.description: We present Cogentic, a multi-agent harness for automated proof discovery on open research problems. While frontier language models can generate strong mathematical ideas in a single shot, single-shot generation is often insufficient for open problems that require exploring multiple competing conjectures, overcoming subtle technical obstructions, and retaining intermediate progress over a long horizon. Cogentic addresses these challenges through an iterative prove--verify loop in which an orchestrator allocates a population of independent provers across distinct proof directions, subjects their output to adversarial verification by several specialized components, and promotes confirmed intermediate results into a persistent verified ledger that later rounds build on. The harness is designed to be able to solve research-level math and theoretical computer science problems. Using Gemini as the base model, Cogentic produced novel results on five open problems across online learning, auction theory, and mechanism design. Each result was independently verified by domain experts and is developed in full in companion papers. We list these results, and new ones as they are verified, at https://sites.google.com/view/cogentic .
candidates.author: Yang Cai, Vineet Gupta, Yanchen Jiang, Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Grigoris Velegkas, Di Wang

candidates.title: MatLoom: Layered Text-to-Material Generation in a Compact Program Space
candidates.description: Material generation should produce not only an appearance, but also the rules that construct it. We introduce MatLoom, a compact, layer-oriented language for text-to-material generation with pretrained language models. Each program composes alpha-masked layers whose shared spatial expressions define coverage and physically based rendering (PBR) channels, making dependencies between patterns, color, and relief explicit. A standalone interpreter evaluates the program into material maps, while the source retains named fields and layer parameters for subsequent authoring. Without task-specific fine-tuning, our pipeline uses parser-guided repair and preview-based critique to revise material designs, then searches noise seeds while keeping each candidate's remaining source fixed. On a curated benchmark of 141 prompts evaluated with six backbones, our best-performing configuration achieves higher mean scores than three diffusion baselines on all four flat-layout prompt-alignment metrics. Its initial programs already exceed all three baselines on mean BLIPScore, before critique or seed search. Retained programs have a median length of 21 lines when pooled across backbones. In a blind four-way comparison involving 30 participants and 20 prompts, our renders receive 59.2% of choices, compared with 19.3% for the most-preferred baseline. Compact executable programs thus offer a way to generate prompt-aligned materials while retaining their construction as part of the asset.
candidates.author: Anson Y. Lam, Shuqing Li, Michael R. Lyu

candidates.title: Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts
candidates.description: Looped transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) offer complementary routes to efficient scaling: recurrence increases computational depth at fixed parameters, while MoE sparsity expands total capacity at fixed active compute. Yet existing scaling laws model recurrence or sparsity in isolation. In this work, we introduce Loop Scaling Laws, the first scaling law to jointly model recurrence and sparsity alongside model size and data. At its core is a bounded, sparsity-conditional recurrence mapping that characterizes the effective-parameter gain from looping and how sparsity raises this gain. The laws predict the held-out loss of looped models more accurately than prior alternatives, and recover the standard dense and MoE scaling laws as special cases. Beyond prediction, the fitted laws provide a principled foundation for designing looped MoE models under compute and memory constraints. Downstream evaluations further demonstrate the complementary benefits of the two axes: sparsity delivers ~3x active-parameter efficiency, recurrence yields ~2x total-parameter efficiency on reasoning, and joint scaling further advances the performance frontier. As a practical extension, we show these gains hold at trillion-token scale: at matched training compute, a looped MoE with law-derived recurrence matches a ~2x larger non-looped MoE on the reasoning benchmarks, while enabling test-time scaling through recurrence.
candidates.author: Yanbei Chen, Anirudh Goyal, Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi

candidates.title: DynaHarness: A Dynamic Physical Harness for Self-Evolving Robot Agents
candidates.description: Pretrained robot policies provide useful action priors, but long-horizon manipulation still requires coordination between semantic reasoning and physical execution. Semantic reasoning operates at a coarser timescale than physical interaction, while episode-level failures provide limited guidance on which system component should be revised. We propose DynaHarness, a dynamic physical harness that couples semantic reasoning with physical governance through a shared execution contract and turns failure evidence into validated capability revisions. To be more specific, the slow brain proposes capabilities and symbolic arguments, while the fast brain grounds and monitors commands, refuses unresolved actions, substitutes capabilities, and requests replans when needed. The physical execution contract bounds each accepted command and records execution evidence across analytic skills, recovery skills, and the frozen VLA. Failure attribution localizes faults in these records and directs targeted revisions of reusable capabilities or execution mechanisms. Paired regression checks govern admission or rejection, closing the self-evolution loop. On LIBERO-Pro, DynaHarness achieves 75.2% on 800 newly sampled initial states, compared with 17.5% for the frozen policy. With the same capability library, full dynamic execution reaches 74.0% versus 63.9% under nominal one-step replanning. This demonstrates the value of DynaHarness as a dynamic physical harness that governs how existing capabilities are grounded, monitored, and coordinated during execution. Our project page is at https://denghaoyuan123.github.io/Dynaharness_page/.
candidates.author: Haoyuan Deng, Jiebin Liu, Tengxiao Zhang, Langning Yan, Hongye Cao, Ziwei Wang
